what_it_does: Easz addresses neural image compression on IoT devices (sensors, edge cameras) with tiny memory and compute budgets. Standard neural compression uses heavy encoder networks on-device that make images uncompressed again, then separate decoder networks—both consume power and storage. Easz shifts the computational burden: the encoder runs on a server with ample power, while the edge device sends only the critical pixels (uses a patch-erase algorithm to decide which pixels to discard) plus a small bit of metadata. The receiver reconstructs the discarded pixels using a lightweight transformer-based decoder (a small neural network) that runs efficiently on-device. Crucially, the system adapts to different compression ratios without retraining—varying the number of patches erased changes compression on the fly.
